sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:85955
Court No. - 73

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 5864 of 2024
Applicant :- Ajay

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Sudhanshu Kumar Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Sri Kameshwar Singh, learned Advocate submits that he is also one of the counsel for the
applicant in the present matter but his name is not shown in the cause list.

2. Heard Sri Kameshwar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Santosh Kumar Nigam,
learned AGA for the State.
3.

The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 65 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 304B, 316 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Bisanda, District Banda during pendency of the trial.

4. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and his family members and according to the FIR marriage of the applicant was performed with the daughter of the informant and after marriage applicant and his family members tortured her for demand of a motorcycle.

It is further mentioned in the FIR that on 18.02.2023 applicant and his family members after committing murder of his daughter thrown her body in the well but due to the bad mental condition, informant Ajay vs State Of U.P. on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165384058/
1 earlier could not lodge the FIR of the present case.

5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that on the basis of false allegation, applicant has been made accused in the present matter and actually deceased due to bad behavior of her father committed suicide by making jump in the well.
6. He further submits that immediately after the incident applicant and his family members along with other persons rushed the deceased to the hospital but unfortunately she could not survive.

He further submits that from perusal of the inquest report, which was conducted on 18.02.2023, it reflects that informant is also one of the Panch witness and at that time he did not raise any objection and after four days he lodged FIR of the present case and this fact shows that FIR is based on false and fabricated facts.

7. He further submits that even from parcha of case diary dated 23.02.2023, which has been annexed as Annexure-6 to the affidavit, it reflects that after receiving information about drowning of his wife in the well, applicant himself consumed poison and after treatment he could survive and this fact shows that applicant was having attachment with his wife and entire allegation with regard to demand of dowry and torture is totally false.
8.
He further submits that from the post mortem report, it reflects that deceased did not sustain any ante mortem injury and died due to drowning.
9. He further submits that applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 11.03.2023 i.e. for last more than a year.
10. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submits that wife of the applicant died under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry.

He further submits that at the time of incident deceased was having pregnancy of five months, therefore, there was hardly any reason for her to commit suicide but he could not dispute the fact that FIR of the present case was lodged after four days and at the time of inquest informant was present and he did not raise any objection at that time.

11. He further could not dispute the fact that from the case diary, it reflects that after receiving information about drowning of the wife, applicant himself consumed poison and after treatment he recovered.
He further could not dispute the fact that in the present matter applicant is in jail since March, 2023 i.e. for last more than a year.
12. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

13. However, applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within nine months of her marriage under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry but it reflects that FIR of the present case was lodged on 22.02.2023 while deceased was died on 18.02.2023 and on same day her inquest was conducted and during inquest informant i.e. father of the deceased was one of Panch witness, therefore, argument advanced by learned counsel for the Ajay vs State Of U.P. on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165384058/
2 applicant that after four days on the basis of false allegation of demand of dowry and torture, FIR of the present case was lodged cannot be completely ruled out at this stage.
14. Further, from the post mortem it reflects that deceased died due to drowning and doctor did not note any ante mortem injury on her person.

Further, post mortem report however suggests that at the time of incident deceased was pregnant and however in general a pregnant lady does not think about to commit suicide but considering the fact that immediately after the incident when applicant came to know about the death of his wife due to drowning then he himself consumed poison and after treatment he could only be survived, his innocence at this stage cannot be ruled out.
15. Further, applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail for last more than a year.

16. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
17. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

18. Let the applicant - Ajay be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
19. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

20. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 13.5.2024 AK Pandey  Ajay vs State Of U.P. on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165384058/
